newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest pharma shares up,MOL down, BUX index flat.
newsitem.headline: Budapest pharma shares up,MOL down, BUX index flat.

text.p: Gainers outnumbered losers on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday but the BUX index remained virtually unchanged.
All eyes were on Hungarian oil and gas company MOL as the government was meeting to decide on the consumer price rise it would allow energy compnies to intoroduce in January.
Its announcement of an 18.8 percent rise in gas prices and 24.9 percent for electricity came too late to affect trading.
MOL, the exclusive supplier of gas to the distributors, saw its stock fall 45 to 1675 forints after rising sharply on Wednesday.
"I think investors thought the rise would be smaller," said Robert Forgo of brokers MKB Ertekpapir. "They thought it would be 16.4 percent and were therefore not as optimistic as yesterday."
Forgo said that in view of the higher-than-expected price hike MOL shares would rise tomorrow.
Andrea Keresztesi of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett also believed MOL would rally on Friday but warned that the rise could still be too low to reap long-term rewards for shareholders.
"The effect of the announcement will be positive tomorrow but as these are consumer price rises we still don't know what MOL will get," she said. "It could be just 10 or 12 percent."
She added that long-term prospects for MOL may not be so rosy if its cut is too low.
Pharmaceutical companies Richter and Egis both saw sharp rises of 1.83 percent and 1.09 percent respectively.
Richter ended 150 up at 8,350 forints while Egis closed at 8,340, up 90.
"Western investors believe both companies have been undervalued in the last few weeks and are showing interest," Forgo said.
